title: Note on Lebesgue's universal cover problem
summary: A universal cover is a convex set that covers all sets of diameter 1 after some rotation, reflection, and translation. First, we show that a regular dodecahedron that circumscribes a ball of diameter 1 is not a universal cover in $\mathbb R^3$, answering a question of Chakerian [K]. Second, we improve the bounds on the minimum volume of a universal cover in $\mathbb R^3$ to $(0.545193,0.655984)$. Third, we give an infinite family of centrally symmetric polytopes in $\mathbb R^d$ with $d(d+1)$ facets that circumscribe the unit ball and are universal covers.
